instructions.value:
Add a word_count(s) function to textutil.py that returns the number of whitespace-separated words in the input string s. Then add comprehensive unit tests in test_textutil.py to verify the function works correctly, including edge cases. The project's test command is `python3 -m unittest -q`.

After implementing, run the test command to verify all tests pass.

When you have finished, call the `report` tool of the marion MCP server exactly once, with a one-sentence `narrative` of what you did. Your final message is not returned to whoever delegated this task; only that report is.

acceptance_criteria.value: word_count function exists in textutil.py and correctly counts whitespace-separated words
Unit tests exist in test_textutil.py covering normal cases and edge cases
All tests pass when running python3 -m unittest -q

narrative.value: Added word_count(s) to textutil.py (len(s.split())) plus 10 edge-case unit tests in test_textutil.py covering empty/whitespace-only input, mixed/unicode whitespace, punctuation and non-ASCII words, and `python3 -m unittest -q` passes all 12 tests (note: the pre-existing last_n_lines has an unrelated off-by-one bug returning n+1 lines, left untouched).

diff --git a/test_textutil.py b/test_textutil.py
index 4b5ccdb..56a26a3 100644
--- a/test_textutil.py
+++ b/test_textutil.py
@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@
 import unittest
 
-from textutil import count_lines
+from textutil import count_lines, word_count
 
 
 class CountLinesTest(unittest.TestCase):
@@ -11,5 +11,37 @@ class CountLinesTest(unittest.TestCase):
         self.assertEqual(count_lines(""), 0)
 
 
+class WordCountTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_single_word(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("hello"), 1)
+
+    def test_multiple_words(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("the quick brown fox"), 4)
+
+    def test_empty(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count(""), 0)
+
+    def test_whitespace_only(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("   \t\n  "), 0)
+
+    def test_leading_and_trailing_whitespace(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("  hello world  "), 2)
+
+    def test_repeated_spaces_between_words(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("a    b     c"), 3)
+
+    def test_mixed_whitespace(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("a\tb\nc\r\nd\x0be\x0cf"), 6)
+
+    def test_unicode_whitespace(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("a\u00a0b\u2003c"), 3)
+
+    def test_punctuation_stays_attached(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("hello, world! it's-fine."), 3)
+
+    def test_non_ascii_words(self):
+        self.assertEqual(word_count("café naïve 日本語"), 3)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()

@@ -10,3 +10,8 @@ def last_n_lines(s, n):
     """Return the last n lines of s, oldest first."""

+
+
+def word_count(s):
+    """Return the number of whitespace-separated words in s."""
+    return len(s.split())
